extracted.intended_audience: patent searchers and IP professionals using Questel.Orbit (e.g., patent librarians, patent attorneys, IP researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and operational standards for conducting patent and bibliographic searches, displaying and printing results, managing saved searches/SDIs, and using special patent/legal features in the Questel.Orbit system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connecting to Questel.Orbit
rubrics_metrics.description: Type the Questel.Orbit network User Address and choose the service from the Welcome menu (I - QUESTEL.ORBIT IMAGES Gif/Tiff; M - MERGED MARKUSH SERVICE (MMS); Q - QUESTEL.ORBIT (TTY/ASCII terminals)). Web access through QWEB: enter QWEB website address, click Login or Secure Login, type Login & Password, click Login.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes choice of protocol (8 BITS - KERMIT etc.) and mode-change options (C to change to 7 BITS), and example login prompts (Logon : XXXXX:XX; Password : XXXX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Logging off / Ending a session
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands and behavior to end a Questel.Orbit session (with or without a temporary saved search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains difference when session has a temporary saved search (two-hour default) and how to properly disconnect to preserve or discard temporary saved searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaccount billing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SUBACCT commands to charge search costs to a particular client/department/project; subaccount names up to 30 alphanumeric characters (no spaces/tabs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands: SUBACCT <name>, SUBACCT to display current, HIS SUBACCT to list charged subaccounts in current session, SUBACCT END to revert to main billing account. Intended to itemize online cost estimator and monthly invoice per subaccount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a database / FILE (FI) command
rubrics_metrics.description: Display list of available databases (FI or FILE) and select a database (e.g., FI PLUSPAT, FI DWPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes database ranging, using FROM parameter to limit commands to a specific database, and how previously-created search strategies are handled when connecting to a cluster (erased). Use ';' to stack commands and FROM to reference previous database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cluster searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Search across system or user-defined database clusters for 'one search' or multi-file search; use CL to create/select clusters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same commands/operators used as for single database; use FROM parameter to limit a command to a single database in a cluster; POP DET ON/OFF changes whether detailed database-by-database results are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting a search to specific updates or date ranges (UP command)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use UP to list and limit searches to specific updates, update numbers, ranges, or years (e.g., UP 1, UP 5-7, UP 2001-2002, UP ALL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: UP uses the date the update is added to the database and does not correspond exactly to the producer update. Use UP FROM <DB> to list updates from a specific database in a cluster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting to a sub-set of the database (LIM command)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a database sub-set with LIM followed by a search statement number or term(s); subsequent searches operate on this subset until LIM ALL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: LIM 3, LIM 2002-37/UP, LIM HOECHST/PA AND JP/PN. Notes: LIM cannot be used in SDI/current awareness searches; limiting to a zero-result statement is ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search term types
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize different types of search terms: single word terms (free text), multi-word phrases (phrase indexed), dates (rangeable date fields, e.g., PD=YYYY-MM-DD), numeric terms (e.g., classification codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct entry: enter terms directly (system default SEARCH MODE). Examples and incorrect entries provided. See NBR command for indexed phrase handling and 'Date Searching'/'Patent Class Searching' sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied adjacency
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain indexes, implied adjacency enables searching without the W proximity operator; right-hand and internal truncation can be used; left-hand truncation not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If middle/internal words are 3 characters or less they will be ignored; use explicit W to retrieve 3-char middle words. Applies only in selected databases/indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truncation (right, left, internal, limited/unlimited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for unlimited truncation and limited truncation (up to one or two characters, or exactly one), right-hand truncation, internal truncation (from second character only), left-hand truncation, and combinations using #, ?, + with limits (each type up to 3 times, limit 7 term portions and identical truncation symbols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ROBOT+, ALUMIN?UM, +INFLAMMATORY, SURF+, /IC H01#. Display options for variations (+CONDUCT+/S). Note limit of 30,000 terms per answer set when using truncation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching with field qualifiers (post- and pre-qualify)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use field qualifiers to search specific indexes/fields (post-qualify: TI PA IN AP PR AB IC PCL CT CLM MCLM; pre-qualify: searches whole statement in specified index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FLD to list valid field qualifiers for current database. Several qualifiers may be used simultaneously; qualifiers can be applied to parentheses; examples: SMITH+/PA/IN, /PA CIBA AND GEIGY.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date and numeric field qualifiers and numeric operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Date fields searchable as year-month-day (PD=YYYY-MM-DD); can specify specific date, before/after/inclusive, ranges; use numeric operators <, >, <=, >=, = for numeric fields (e.g., NCL>=5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Link (L) operator to specify a date with a specific patent authority/country (e.g., /PN US L 2002). Single numeric fields include family member counts, number of claims, number of drawings. Presence flags: CT=YES, UAB=YES.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining terms and proximity operators; parentheses and nesting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) and proximity operators W, nW, =nW, D, nD, =nD to combine terms; presence operators for sentence (S), paragraph (P), link (L), field (F); negation in paragraph/linked/sentence/field via NOTP/NOTL/NOTS/NOTF; parentheses for nesting (up to 5 levels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NEW W YORK, FILTER 3W FLOW, METAL W METAL 3W BOND, COMPOSITE? (=1D) (FIBRE? OR FIBER?). Use spaces or parentheses for operators; end long lines with space + hyphen '-' to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching character strings (STRS)
rubrics_metrics.description: STRS searches specified character strings in the Basic Index (default) or specific fields, with truncation and operators allowed; default searches last search statement's result set (max 5000 records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: STRS CILLIN, STRS CILLIN /IT, STRS CILL # N, STRS CILLIN OR CILLAN. Use STRS SS 3 CILL # N /IT to combine parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displaying the number of results and POP options
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of results is automatically displayed in single-db environment; cluster environment displays total across cluster. Use POP options to control displays (e.g., POP DET ON/OFF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands such as POP AUDIT ON, POP DET OFF; default is to display detailed results for each database in cluster (DET ON).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulating the search strategy (FLD, NBR, HIS, ER, KEEP, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands to view fields/indexes (FLD), check nearest indexed terms (NBR), view history (HIS), erase/delete search statements (ER), keep specific statements (KEEP), display search strategy in full or by range, and display indexes/terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: FLD FROM PLUSPAT, NBR COLOR, HIS 5-8, ER 3, ER 3-6 8, ER ALL. If a search finds zero results, use NBR to check nearest terms. ERASE options include deleting last statement, deleting from a specific SS number, deleting several statements, zero-result statements, or strategies from previously selected databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online display formats (system-defined and user-defined)
rubrics_metrics.description: System-defined display formats include SC/SCAN (AN,TI), TR (AN,TI,indexing), TEST (minimum), STDR (default), FULL or MAX (complete record). Users may also create user-defined formats and tailor displays with specific fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands: PRT SCAN, PRT TR, PRT TEST, PRT STDR, PRT MAX. Can combine system formats and specific fields or exclude fields. Default display is the first record in STDR format from the last search statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing images (IMG parameter and image display options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Access images in selected patent/trademark databases by choosing 'I' from Welcome menu, adding IMG parameter to PRT command, or selecting 'I' in BR/FO commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands: IM, IM5 to select documents containing images; PRT IMG, PRT MAX IMG, PRT 1-25 NONSTOP. To receive images in email offline prints include RTF and IMG parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of lines option (POP NL / OP NL) and display continuity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of records displayed is set by POP NL (default 24 lines); behavior differs by Welcome menu mode (Q or I). If NL <= 100 default display uses NL; if NL > 100 default displays first record only unless range specified; in 'I' mode default is first record only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NONSTOP parameter and specify ranges for continuous displays. POP NL 50, POP NL 500 examples. Also configure number of characters per line POP NC.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOCUS, BROWSE and KWIC display options
rubrics_metrics.description: BRowse displays records one by one (BR); FOcus displays records with surrounding context of search term(s) (default three lines around term); KWIC (Key Words In Context) displays continuous results with 1 line before and after search terms and can be used in place of PRT or FO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: BR SS 8, FO SS 2, KWIC TEST, KWIC TEST 5-10. KWIC [free format] is free; if non-basic index fields are shown it may incur charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEGAL feature for patent/legal displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Use LEGAL option when printing to automatically display corresponding legal records from other databases (e.g., LEGALUS, LEGALEP, LEGALIFI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEGAL options: LEGAL (from LGST), LEGAL MAXE, LEGALUS (CRXX,LITA), LEGALEP (EPPATENT), LEGALIFI, LEGALERT (LITA), LEGALALL, LEGALLCL. Examples: PRT 1 LEGAL MAXE, PRT 1-10 LEGALUS.

rubrics_metrics.name: CITEd feature (displaying corresponding citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: CITEd is a display option (not to be confused with CITF/CITB commands) that extracts Cited data from databases for display with records that may lack citation data; options include CITEP, CITPCT, CITFR, CITUS, CITEPPCT, CITALL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: PRT CITUS, PRT CITEP, PRT CITEPPCT. Use to print selected records or entire sets. NOTE: distinct from automatic citation-searching commands (CITF/CITB).

rubrics_metrics.name: FULL Feature (full-text and full-claims display)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add EP, WO, and US fulltext or claims when displaying records in biblio databases by using FULL features (FULLEPO, FULLWO, FULLUS, FULLTEXT, FULLCLMS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fulltext files available: EPAPAT (EP fulltext from 1978 onward), PCTFULL (PCT from 1978 onward), USPAT (US from 1971 onward). Examples: PRT MAX FULLEPO, PRT ABST 1-5 FULLWO, PRT FULL 1 3 5-8 FULLUS CLMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLUS feature (adding fields/formats from other files)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRT <FORMAT> <N-N or SET> PLUS <FIELD/FORMAT> (FILE NAME) allows adding fields or formats from other files via automatic cross-filing of standardized patent numbers (XPNs) and integration below each corresponding document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: PRT STDR 1-9 PLUS EC (PLUSPAT), PRT BIB SET PLUS CLMS (EPAPAT). Use PLUS with images: PRT IMG MAX SET PLUS STDR (EPAPAT). One format name may be system-defined or user-defined; field label cannot be used as format name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family searching (FAM command and syntax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Family searching in databases PLUSPAT, INPD, DWPI, etc., by publication (PN), application (AP) or priority (PR) numbers using syntax: FAM CCNNNNNNN/PN, FAM YYYYCC-NNNNNNN/AP, FAM YYYYCC-NNNNNNN/PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC = country code; examples: FAM EP---160/PN, FAM 1997EP-0100811/AP, FAM 1997DE-1020719/PR. Standardized numbers allow family searching across listed databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAMSTAT / MFAMSTAT / Merged family display commands
rubrics_metrics.description: FAMSTAT prints patent family records from INPADOC or PLUSPAT and corresponding LGST legal status records; MFAMSTAT in PlusPat displays merged family data, abstract with legal status in one integrated record; Merged Family Print integrates individual family members into one virtual family display (limit 1000 records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FAMSTAT immediately after FAM; options: FAMSTATE, FAMSTAT MAXE, FAMLIST, MFAMSTAT, MFAMSTATE. For merged family display: use FAM SS <n> then PRT MINI SET or PRT MMAX 1-3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating a database cluster (CL command) and managing clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Create user-defined database clusters (CL <name> <dbs>) up to 40 databases per cluster and up to 12 clusters per UserID; list, select, and delete clusters; ID and ID STAT commands show cluster status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CL PAT1 DWPI EPPATENT JAPIO ; CL PAT1 ; FI CL PATENTS. Use ID to reorder files in cluster and obtain list of databases in a cluster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and deduping results (ID command and print options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group cluster results into patent groups (records describing same invention) and display options for groups: first record, duplicates only, all except duplicates, groups with >1 record, single-record groups; use ID command to group and reorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display/grouping commands: PRT GR SET, PRT GR SET FIRST, PRT GR SET NODUP, PRT PATGR SET, PRT PATGR FIRST, PRT PATGR NODUP, PRT PATGR DUPLI, PRT PATGR MATCH, etc. Provides counts of groups, duplicates, singles.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPUB (merge publication stages)
rubrics_metrics.description: MPUB gathers all publication stages of the same patent and integrates them into one merged record (available in DEPAT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax examples: MPUB DE4210167/PN, MPUB 1994DE-4423677/AP, MPUB 1998US-0111106/PR, MPUB SS 1. Note: limit of 1000 results per SS when creating merged records from a set. Display via PRT MPS or PRT MPMX.

rubrics_metrics.name: CITF and CITB (forward and backward citation searches)
rubrics_metrics.description: CITF runs a forward citation search on a set of records (retrieves patents citing the initial set); CITB runs a backward citation search (retrieves patents cited by the initial set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available in EPPATENT, FRPATENT, WOPATENT, USPAT, DEPAT & PLUSPAT. Commands operate on a set of results (use HIS to find SS); max initial set size is 1000 results per SS. Use FROM parameter to target a specific DB in cluster (e.g., CITF SS 1 FROM EPPATENT).

rubrics_metrics.name: FAMCITE (family citation report)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAMCITE creates a citation report for a patent family showing the original source family, citing patent families, and cited patent families; optional IMG parameter to include clipped images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after a family search for a single patent family (in PlusPat). Commands: FAMCITE, FAMCITE IMG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offline printing by email (PR EMAIL) and format options
rubrics_metrics.description: Order email delivery of documents (default: docs from last search statement in MAX ASCII, limited to 500 docs per order); stored email address required on ID; formats supported: RTF, XML, PDF (with accents/special characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To receive images include RTF and IMG parameters. Documents sent within one hour of order. Commands: PR EMAIL XML, PR EMAIL RTF IMG, SET EMAIL, PR EMAIL;SET.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offline print by mail (ordering options and defaults)
rubrics_metrics.description: Order offline prints mailed to stored postal address (default max 5000 records from last search statement in MAX format). Each order assigned a reference number; defaults differ for single-db vs cluster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: specify format (system/user-defined), specific fields, record ranges, page layout, include images, combine parameters. Must set AD postal address before ordering. Sorting options and alternate addresses supported. Cancel using order reference number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevancy ranking of search results (RK command)
rubrics_metrics.description: Display search results in order of relevance (descending order of occurrence of search terms); results stored in SS 203 for display; RK works on max 5000 records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands: RK, RK SS 5, RK SS 2 FROM DWPI. Use FROM in clusters to rank results from a specific DB. RK stores results in SS 203.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online sorting (SORT command) and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort records by specific field(s) into SS 203 for display/printing/crossfile searching. Sorting supports up to 3 fields (max total sort key 100 chars) and defaults for text/dates/numeric lengths and directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults: text ascending (+), dates/numeric descending (–). Sorting limits: up to ~5000 records. Examples: SORT /IN, SORT SS 3 /IN, SORT /PAN RK 2, SORT /PN PRG 1 RK 4. Position (rank) parameters (RK) and PRG position used for specifying the sort key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossfile searching and memory lists (MEM, MEMS, GET, statistical analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract terms and save in memory lists for crossfile searching and statistical analysis; default memory lists MEM1-MEM4; *MEM super-terms support searching terms in memory (MEM super-term).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands: MEM, MEMS, GET, MEMSORT, SEL. Number of terms per memory list: 100,000. MEM1 default crossfile; MEM2 default statistical list. Statistical analysis with GET macro and MEMS super-terms; MEMS searchable with *MEMS super-term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saved searches and SDIs (temporary & permanent saved searches; set sdi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for temporary saved searches (two-hour default) and permanent saved searches; SDI (current awareness) profiles can be created/modified via set sdi commands with many parameters (files, updates, print/display command, title, subaccount, email, format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Commands: SAVE name, STORE name, set sdi =, set sdi ; pr , set sdi ; ti , set sdi ; email
!. Delivery formats: PDF, RTF, TXT, XML. Page styles and display formats configurable. SDIs can include PLUS.

rubrics_metrics.name: User options (postal/email, permanent/temporary options, ordering documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage permanent user options (accented characters, nl, nc, language, truncation display, highlighting, processing message frequency, image format, MFAM preference), temporary session options (OP commands), and ordering documents via PDS (ORDER EXPO XPN ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands: AD to set postal address, SET EMAIL to store email, PDS order allows up to 10 PNs. POP and OP commands to modify permanent/temporary options. FROM parameter required/optional with specific commands in cluster environments (essential with JOIN, MEMS, RK, SO, SAVE, STORE, SDI, OR, UP; optional with BR, FLD, FO, FOR, HIS, PRT, MEM).

rubrics_metrics.name: JOIN and *MDARC (linking Questel.Orbit and MMS / Markush DARC integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: JOIN transfers chemical compound numbers from bibliographic records (DWPI, PHARM) to chemical structure files (WPAM, MPHARM); *MDARC super-terms transfer numbers in the reverse direction to Questel.Orbit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphical terminal emulation required for MARKUSH DARC. Default transfers all compound numbers in last search statement (max 5,000; up to 50,000 for MPHARM). Examples: JOIN TO WPAM VIA LIST3 SPE, *MDARC NAME1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserved terms handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Questel.Orbit commands and system/proximity operators are reserved terms (e.g., IMAGE, ID, PRINT, FILE, W, D, F, S, P, L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workarounds: truncation, word order (place reserved term second), or quotes to retrieve exact reserved term as a search term (e.g., "IMAGE" OR WATERMARK).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopwords behavior (file-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain files (DWPI, IFIPAT, PHARM, CAS) have stopwords associated with chemical symbols; words are treated as stopwords only if they begin with a lower-case letter (e.g., a, at, be, he, in, and, no).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To search phrases with 'in' in stopword-free files use double quotes: "IN" W VITRO. For DWPI/IFIPAT/PHARM/CAS drop the word 'in' from the search request or use quoting workarounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: System limits
rubrics_metrics.description: System-imposed limits: number of search statements per database 200; characters per search statement 2,030; terms per answer set using truncation 30,000; terms per memory list 100,000; number of types of truncation within a search term 3; number of term portions/identical truncation symbols 7; default memory lists 4 (150 user-named lists); grouping/sorting/ranking limits typically 5000 documents; family searches on a search set FAM SS limit 1000; proximity word limit with w/d is 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and numeric limits are given throughout: MPUB/Group/Sort/RK commands max 5000; FAM SS max 1000; Truncation and memory list caps detailed. Be aware these operational limits when composing complex searches or ordering offline prints (max 5000 by postal mail, 500 by email).
